steps.title: 2021: before the full-scale war
text: In 2021 [Ukraine](UKR) exported **$65.8 billion** of goods. Its largest customers were [China](CHN) (12%), [Poland](POL) (8%) and [Türkiye](TUR) (6%).
Agriculture and food made up 40% of its exports and base metals 24% (CEPII BACI). The map shows where Ukraine's exports went.

steps.title: February 2022: invasion
text: On **24 February 2022** [Russia](RUS) launched a full-scale invasion of [Ukraine](UKR). In March and April Ukraine's exports were about half their level a year earlier (−49% and **−50%**).
For 2022 as a whole they fell 32% to $44.5 billion, and real GDP shrank **28.8%**. The map shows the change in exports to each partner from the same month a year earlier.

steps.title: Grain finds new routes
text: From July 2022 to **17 July 2023** the Black Sea Grain Initiative, signed in Istanbul, allowed commercial food and fertilizer exports from three Ukrainian ports: Odesa, Chornomorsk and Yuzhny/Pivdennyi.

Wheat exports still fell, from $6.3 billion in 2021 to $3.8 billion in 2022, but maize held up ($6.3 billion). Its buyers changed: [China](CHN)'s share fell from 32% to **17%**, while [Romania](ROU) took 14% and [Spain](ESP) 12%. EU countries are shown separately here: watch the maize arcs shift towards them.

steps.title: From steel to farm goods
text: Base metals fell from 24% of [Ukraine](UKR)'s exports in 2021 to **10%** in 2024, from $17.1 billion to $4.8 billion. Agriculture and food rose from 40% to **59%**.
The highlighted list in the panel re-sorts as the timeline plays (CEPII BACI).

steps.title: Closer to the EU
text: From **4 June 2022** the [EU](EU) suspended import duties, quotas and trade defence measures on Ukrainian goods; the measures were renewed until 5 June 2025.
The EU's share of [Ukraine](UKR)'s exports rose from 39% in 2021 to **63%** in 2022, and was 58% in 2024. In 2022 [Poland](POL) alone bought 15%.

steps.title: Imports came back, exports did not
text: [Ukraine](UKR)'s imports were $70.5 billion in 2024, about the same as in 2021 ($70.0 billion), while its exports were $40.2 billion. Its trade deficit grew from $4.1 billion in 2021 to **$30.3 billion** in 2024.
[China](CHN) supplied 20% of Ukraine's imports in 2024, up from 15%. The highlighted panel section shows the gap opening between exports and imports.
